messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue growth > 95% for cluster/us-west-2/gpu-pool for 5m, HPA target not increasing. Alert: gpu_queue_growth_high (see: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2770004444)

emma (oncall): paging. I’m on it, digging into dashboards now.

ben: seeing the same on our side — queue length jumped ~6x starting 12:02 UTC, pods are at 100% utilization and OOM throttling spikes. HPA metrics show 0 additional desired replicas.

dinesh: can someone check the custom metrics adapter? prometheus-adapter has been flapping earlier today. last scrape backlog spike at 11:58.

carla (sre): `kubectl get hpa -n inference gpu-workers -o yaml` -> desiredReplicas: 0, currentReplicas: 8, metrics: custom/fake_gpu_queue: targetAverageValue: 1000, currentAverageValue: 6000. HPA controller logs show "could not get metrics" errors.

ben: paste logs from prometheus-adapter:
```
I0312 12:05:01.123 PromAdapter] query_range failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
I0312 12:05:01.124 PromAdapter] failing to fetch custom metrics for HPA: 503
```

maria (support): customers reporting increased 5xxs and long generation times. Ticket stream shows ~12 affected tenants (mostly mid-tier dedicated clusters). Escalated to priority.

emma (oncall): quick impact note: ingress queue growth leads to per-request latency > 10s and some 503s when requests hit throttle. Not full outage but degraded for higher qps routes. Notify CS and execs with initial RCA-in-progress.

carla (sre): likely root cause path: prometheus scrape backlog -> adapter timeouts -> HPA cannot read custom GPU queue length -> desiredReplicas stays flat -> pods saturate -> queue grows -> ingress starts throttling requests.

dinesh: confirm metrics pipeline: node exporters -> prometheus -> prometheus-adapter -> metrics-server/HPA. If adapter is delayed, HPA has no signal. Also saw adapter restarted 3x earlier (11:40-11:55) due to mem pressure on metrics-ns.

emma (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) force scale up to relieve immediate pressure 2) triage adapter & restart with larger mem limit 3) enable fallback HPA policy (use cpu-based target) for gpu-workers until adapter stabilized 4) rate-limit heavy tenants as stop-gap.

ben: executing step 1 now: `kubectl scale deployment gpu-workers -n inference --replicas=20` (manual scale to add capacity).

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook matched: GPU_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTION -> step 1: manual scale applied, step 2: check adapter health, step 3: apply fallback HPA. Link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/gpu-capacity-exhaustion

carla (sre): confirming new replicas coming up. pod/gpu-worker-19 failing image pull? no, slow to pass readiness due to long model warm-up. Adding replicas helps queue but warm-up takes ~45s per pod.

emma (oncall): apply fallback HPA now: patch HPA to add cpu metric with conservative target to allow autoscale while adapter is down. `kubectl patch hpa gpu-workers -n inference --type='json' -p='[ {"op":"add","path":"/spec/metrics/-","value":{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","targetAverageUtilization":60}} } ]'`

ben: patch applied. HPA desiredReplicas changed to 18 within 2m. queue trend flattening.

maria (support): posting customer status: "We’re aware of degraded performance affecting some inference requests in US-West. Engineers are actively mitigating; some customers may see increased latency for several minutes." Posted to affected tenants.

dinesh: restarting prometheus-adapter with increased memory: `kubectl set resources deployment prometheus-adapter -n metrics --limits=memory=1Gi --requests=512Mi` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n metrics`

carla (sre): adapter pods restarted and are healthy (12:24 UTC). adapter logs now show normal scrape rates and successful queries.

ben: HPA now picking up custom metric again: currentAverageValue dropping back toward target. HPA recommended desiredReplicas slowly ramping down to stable range 10-12.

emma (oncall): tip: because warm-up is slow we should consider pre-warming model cache next time or use smaller model variant as fallback. For now keep manual replica cap at 15 for 10m to avoid oscillations.

carla (sre): applied `kubectl annotate deployment/gpu-workers redwood/hold-scale=true` as a temporary guard and set `kubectl scale --replicas=15` to cap.

maria (support): update: second wave of customers report improvements; ticket backlog decreasing. Will send a full customer impact summary after incident.

emma (oncall): post-mitigations checklist: - monitor HPA metrics for 30m - verify no further adapter restarts - follow up with infra to increase adapter resources in next release - prepare postmortem & notify PM/ops leadership.

dinesh: will open a follow-up PR to bump prometheus-adapter mem & add liveness/readiness thresholds, and add alert: adapter_restarts_per_5m > 2 -> pager.

carla (sre): note for RCA: we saw memory pressure on metrics namespace; possible correlation with large scrape cardinality (many per-tenant exporters). Need longer-term: reduce cardinality or run a dedicated adapter replica set per region.

sre-runbook-bot: Incident resolved -> status: degraded -> mitigated. Please create incident postmortem and label severity: Sev2.

emma (oncall): handing over to carla for postmortem + timeline. on-call handoff to evening shift in 25m. tagging @dinesh @ben for follow-ups.

carla (sre): acknowledged, will draft timeline and root cause hypothesis. moving thread to incident doc draft. :white_check_mark:

maria (support): Closing customer-facing update: "Issue mitigated — normal performance restored for affected routes in US-West. Engineering identified and mitigated an adapter resource issue; follow-up includes capacity & alerts improvements." Will send at 13:05 UTC.

emma (oncall): final note: total duration (alert->mitigated) ~27m. No data loss, degraded latency & some 5xxs for higher-tier tenants. Actions: resource bump, new adapter restart alert, HPA fallback policy/runner, pre-warm strategy.

carla (sre): thanks team. Creating the postmortem doc now and will assign owners for each action item.

incidents-bot: Incident closed in channel. Reference: incident-2770004444
